verdict.label: HOLD — AI-Memory Bid vs. a 1,400 Won: Own SK Hynix, Not the Index, Into CPI
verdict.rationale_short: The KOSPI is caught between two forces pulling in opposite directions. The tailwind is real and Korea-specific: the same AI capital rotation that is draining crypto is flooding into HBM memory, and SK Hynix — the lead supplier of high-bandwidth memory to Nvidia — is the cleanest beneficiary in Asia, holding green while global risk sells off. The headwinds are macro and just as real: Friday's hot US jobs print pushed the dollar and US yields higher, the won is sliding toward the psychologically critical 1,400/USD line, foreign investors turned net sellers of KOSPI, and an oil spike from the US-Iran conflict is a direct tax on an energy-importing, export-driven economy. HOLD at medium conviction: this is a stock-pickers' tape, not an index buy. Own the AI-memory leaders (SK Hynix, and Samsung on weakness) and avoid the broad index and won-sensitive exporters until May US CPI on June 10 clears and USD/KRW holds below 1,400. A won break above 1,400 with a hot CPI would force a step-aside on the whole market.

supporting_data.label: KOSPI is holding up better than global peers because the index is ~one-third semiconductors; the AI-driven HBM memory super-cycle is a Korea-specific tailwind even as broad risk sells off — SK Hynix is the lead HBM supplier to Nvidia
The won is sliding toward 1,400/USD as Friday's 172K US payrolls print pushed the dollar (DXY ~99.3) and US yields (30Y above 5.0%) higher — a weak won pressures foreign returns and the Bank of Korea
Foreign investors turned net sellers of KOSPI in the risk-off; foreign flow is the single most important swing factor for Korean equities and the tell for whether the AI-memory bid can offset macro
The US-Iran conflict near Hormuz and the resulting oil spike are a direct headwind for Korea, a net energy importer whose trade balance and inflation are oil-sensitive
Next macro binary for Korean risk: May US CPI on June 10 sets the dollar/yield path that drives USD/KRW and foreign flows; a hot print confirms higher-for-longer and risks a won break above 1,400

trade_setups.thesis: USD/KRW near 1,400 is the swing variable for foreign-currency returns. With the dollar firm and US CPI June 10 unresolved, an unhedged USD investor in KOSPI is also short the won at the worst moment. Hedge the currency or size EWY smaller until 1,400 holds.

bear_case: Korea is a high-beta, FX-sensitive, export-driven market, and right now it faces a triple headwind: a strong dollar that is dragging the won toward 1,400, a global risk-off led by a hot US labor market and 30Y yields above 5.0%, and an oil spike from the US-Iran conflict that taxes an energy importer directly. The semiconductor concentration that is the index's tailwind today is also its single biggest risk — a third of the KOSPI rides on one AI-memory narrative, and if HBM pricing or Nvidia's capex blinks, the relative-strength leader becomes the relative-weakness epicenter. Foreign investors, already net sellers, set the marginal price; a decisive USD/KRW break above 1,400 typically accelerates outflows in a self-reinforcing loop. Invalidation level: a hot May US CPI on June 10 that drives USD/KRW through 1,400 and the KOSPI below 3,150 turns this HOLD into a STEP ASIDE on the whole market; conversely, a cool CPI with the won holding below 1,400 and foreign buyers returning reopens a broad-index long.
